minutes.headline: Planning Board reorganized its officers and committee seats, then continued all three hearings on its agenda.
minutes.summary: The board re-elected its chair, vice chair and clerk, and filled committee representative seats by nomination. It approved an ANR plan for 1 Crocker, and continued the Northfield/Holmen stormwater hearing, the 260 Falulah Road warehouse hearing and the 43 Summer Street hearing. The director also raised a scenic-road stone wall dispute on Flat Hill Road and a pole petition that reached the Select Board first.

budget_items.what_was_said: The planner said the town has received brownfields assessment services through EPA grants administered by MRPC for the gas station site at 925 Mass Ave.
The planner said the town submitted a planning assistance grant with MRPC, funded by the state, to run over roughly two years if awarded.

decisions.decision: The 43 Summer Street hearing, continued at the applicant's request, was set for June 13th.
The 260 Falulah Road hearing will stay open until the Fitchburg approvals are further along.
Next meetings set for June 13th (with a public hearing for 494 Electric Ave) and June 27th.
The planner agreed to look into improved checks so scenic road matters reach the board before other boards act.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued all three hearings on its agenda: Northfield Road/Holmen Street stormwater, 260 Falulah Road, and 43 Summer Street.
The 260 Falulah Road warehouse hearing was continued to July 11th and will stay open until the Fitchburg approvals are further along.
The board approved an ANR plan for 1 Crocker, a lot split across Leominster and Lunenburg, by voice vote.
The board re-elected its chair, vice chair and clerk and filled committee representative seats by nomination, all by voice vote with no count.
The director raised a scenic-road stone wall dispute on Flat Hill Road and a pole petition; the planner agreed to look into checks so such matters reach the board first.

why_it_matters: The Northfield/Holmen stormwater permit and the Falulah Road warehouse stay undecided, so neighbors keep their chance to comment at the continued hearings.
Scenic-road work and utility pole petitions can move ahead at other boards before the Planning Board sees them, and a change to that process would affect how residents on those roads are heard.
watch_next: June 13th: the Northfield/Holmen and 43 Summer Street hearings resume at 6:05, along with a public hearing for 494 Electric Ave.
July 11th: the 260 Falulah Road hearing resumes at 6:05 p.m.
